title: Descending a separable minimal polynomial and its Bezout identity
statement: Let A be an integral domain, K its fraction field, and L a field extension of K with compatible A-algebra structure [def-pc-field-extension]. Let alpha in L be algebraic over K [def-weil-algebraic-element], with separable minimal polynomial p in K[T] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. There exist a nonzero c in A, an A-subalgebra S of L identified with A[c^{-1}] [def-weil-ring-localization-away], an injective ring map phi:S to K whose composition with K to L is the inclusion S to L, and a monic f in S[T] whose image under phi is p and such that f is coprime with its derivative.

source.place: finite-algebra spreading calculation, clearing denominators in the minimal polynomial; realized by parent node step 2

proof.text: Let p be the minimal polynomial of alpha and choose u,v with u*p+v*p' = 1 from separability. Use IsLocalization.integerNormalization_spec on p,u,v to obtain polynomials over A equal to nonzero A-multiples of them. Let c be the product of those three nonzero multipliers.

Construct the injective localization map A[1/c] to K and compose it into L. Let S be its image in L, and use the range equivalence to transfer the localization structure. Its inverse followed by the map to K gives phi:S to K compatible with the inclusion into L.

Each of the three multipliers is invertible in S since their product c is invertible. Multiply each integer-normalized polynomial by the inverse multiplier to obtain f,uS,vS over S. Their images under phi are p,u,v. Injectivity of phi implies f is monic and uS*f+vS*f' = 1, proving coprimality. All these calculations are implemented in Lean.
